mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals tightening monetary policy, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.2% in a month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that suppresses economic growth and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation, which increases equity risk premiums and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.1% m/m, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market tightness that pressures wage growth and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions when UNRATE declines by more than 0.1% in a month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand for housing and broader economic activity, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 60% of instances when HOUST increases by more than 0.5% m/m, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index base 2017=100) for two consecutive months, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100 for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery phases, a month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% signals strong consumer spending momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in less than 60% of instances during post-recession recovery when RSAFS > 0.5% m/m, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor market is strengthening (PAYEMS rising) and industrial production is contracting (INDPRO falling), it signals a supply-demand mismatch that increases inflationary pressures and corporate cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS rises and INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% m/m, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
